lines.text: Conclusion, section two. The habits that matter most.
If you leave this book with only five habits, make it these.
One: before every early-street decision, ask which shape your range wants to be, polarized, condensed, or linear.
Two: before every barrel, sort the incoming turn or river card into good, bad, or neutral for your range.
Three: pick your bet size to grow the pot geometrically toward the future bet you actually want to make.
Four: build your ranges from pure strategies first and use mixed strategies to balance them, so that the load-bearing hands drive the plan.
Five: check SPR and ICM context before you commit chips, because the value of every future action depends on them.
None of these habits is glamorous, and none of them wins a specific hand.
But apply them together, over thousands of hands, and you will find yourself in the right shape at the right time much more often than the players you are competing with.
Range construction is a lifetime skill, not a chapter to be finished, and the toolkit you built here is meant to keep sharpening as you use it.
